what_this_is: The Workshop rows for generate-and-judge-sound-effects: scripts the person's AI runs on the person's own computer to find free sound effects with their licences, judge sound-effect candidates by ear with earshot the way a palette is judged, make and check the palette, place cues into an effects layer and score soundtrack variants, and fit music windows to a loudness arc. The candidates themselves are made by tools/media-composition's make-pictures-and-sounds styles.

payload.label: Judge sound-effect candidates by ear and pick one per sound (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Judge the sound effects I generated or found the way my palette was judged, pick the best one for each sound and level it to my real sound
payload.description: Every candidate (forged, generated by a local model, or downloaded) is trimmed (an event found by earshot with clean edges, or the whole sound for swells), put in the palette format (rate, channels, fades, peak), and read by earshot: match z for the sound's query, realness, measure. A lead-in (a riser) is cut so its peak sits where the real one peaks. The pick is the highest match z among candidates that are not distorted; a sound may be barred from another sound's source. The pick is scaled to the real sound's active loudness and compared with it (A/B). The tuned values can come from the person's settings record (settings_record).

request.description: REQUEST.json (sounds, palette, reference_folder, candidates, group_of, about, lead_in, whole, not_from_pick_of, max_saturated, least_build, candidates_folder, picked_folder, scores, selection, settings_record), put where {request} is

sounds.description: Only these sounds, judged again and merged into the earlier picks; empty for all

output_schema.description: Progress lines, then a last line {"result": {...}} or {"error": "what to change"}.

get_it: install earshot into a Python environment (its own README); run the script with that Python
needs: earshot (the sound-judging Python package, with its listening models) in the Python that runs this
the candidates and the real palette sounds on this computer
invoke.say: Run from the Workshop checkout with the Python that has earshot. Build REQUEST.json from the person's files; its tuned values may come from their settings record (settings_record: the record:setting row of this tool as records:read answers it). Read the last line: { result } names the selection file and each sound's pick; { error } says which sound has no clean candidate.

payload.label: Rank sound effects in folders by ear and find each one's cleanest trim (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Rank my sound-effect folders against a description and find the cleanest trim of the best ones
payload.description: Per category (folder, query, kind, top, alternatives: the person's CATEGORIES.json), earshot ranks the folder, finds the best segments of the top candidates, moves each trim edge outward in 5 ms steps until it is at or below -30 dB of the trim's peak, then describes, judges realness and measures that trim. Merges into OUT.json.

output_schema.description: Progress lines, then a last line {"result": {...}} or {"error": "what to change"}.

payload.label: Judge one-shot sounds as whole sounds (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Judge these one-shot sound files whole, from first onset to their tail, against a description
payload.description: Trim = first onset (-40 dB of peak) less 5 ms to the last sample above -50 dB of peak, then earshot match (against the alternatives), describe, realness and measure on that trim; merged into OUT.json keyed by file and query.

output_schema.description: Progress lines, then a last line {"result": {...}} or {"error": "what to change"}.

payload.label: Make a sound-effect palette from trimmed sources and read each sound back (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Render my sound-effect palette from its sources and trims, and check each finished sound by ear
payload.description: Each sound of PALETTE.json: decode its source at the palette's rate and channels, cut the trim, fade in and out, scale to the sample peak, write 24-bit WAV; then earshot reads the final file (match z, describe, realness, measure) into palette_readings.json.

payload.label: Check a sound-effect palette against its spec and licences (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Check that every sound in my palette has the right format, length, quiet edges and an allowed licence
payload.description: Every rendered palette file against PALETTE.json: rate, channels, sample peak, fade edges, length equal to the trim, and a licence entry in the manifest that is not blocked; music files given have the palette's rate and channels and last long enough. Exit 1 on any failure.

payload.description: Freesound's public search pages, CC0 and Attribution only, within each category's length, most downloaded first; each item once per category. One request every 1.5 s; pages are read as text.

payload.label: Download chosen free sound effects with their licences (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Download the sound effects I chose, reading each one's licence first and keeping a manifest
payload.description: Each selected Freesound item's licence is read on its own page first: only CC0, CC BY 3.0 and CC BY 4.0 are downloaded, the rest recorded as blocked; Mixkit items under its free licence. Every entry (page, author, title, licence as read, description excerpt, date, address, local file) goes to the manifest.

payload.label: Find the stretch of each music track that follows my film's loudness arc (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Find in each candidate music track the window whose loudness follows my film's arc
payload.description: Each track's smoothed loudness curve is compared with the brief's arc (Pearson correlation of dB curves) plus measured constraints (the open below the lift, the swell near the top); the best window of each track is cut as an excerpt.

output_schema.description: Progress lines, then a last line {"result": {...}} or {"error": "what to change"}.

payload.label: Listen to music excerpts against my film's sections (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Judge each music excerpt by ear against my film's section words and a reference stem
payload.description: Per excerpt: per-section mood match against the film's section words (against alternatives), typicality against a reference music stem cut into its sections, realness and the top describe tags.

payload.label: Place a cue plan's sound effects into one effects track (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Lay every sound-effect cue of my cue plan at its time and gain into one effects-only track
payload.description: Every cue [seconds, sound, gain dB] placed at its whole millisecond, with its gain, summed, as a mixer that delays by whole milliseconds places it, with no music and no voice; prints its integrated loudness.

output_schema.description: Progress lines, then a last line {"result": {...}} or {"error": "what to change"}.

payload.label: Give a variant sound palette one gain so its effects track is as loud as the reference (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Scale my variant sound palette by one common gain so its effects track has the reference track's loudness
payload.description: The variant palette's layer over the cue plan is measured, and every sound in it scaled by the one gain that brings it to the reference layer's integrated loudness, so per-sound balance and cue gains stay and a listener compares the sounds, not the level.

payload.label: Score soundtrack variants of a film by ear at every cue (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Score my film's soundtrack variants with earshot: critique, sync to the picture, and how well each sound effect reads at its cue
payload.description: Each variant: earshot critique against the launch profile with the picture, timeline sync to the picture's cuts and the cue frames, realness, and a match z at every cue on the effects layer alone and in the full mix; merged into the scores file.
